title: A Noetherian scheme receiving a finite surjective morphism from an affine scheme is affine
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that (1) $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], (2) $f$ is surjective, i.e. $|Y|\to|X|$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], (3) $Y$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], and (4) $X$ is Noetherian, i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Then $X$ is an affine scheme.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YQ (label lemma-image-affine-finite-morphism-affine-Noetherian, coherent.tex line 3557), with its proof (H^1(X,F)=0 for every coherent F by the devissage Lemma lemma-property-higher-rank-cohomological, using Lemma lemma-finite-morphism-Noetherian, lemma-affine-morphism-projection-ideal, lemma-quasi-coherent-affine-cohomology-zero and lemma-relative-affine-cohomology; then X affine by Serre's criterion, Lemma 01XF lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-covering or lemma-quasi-separated-h1-zero-covering)

proof.text: Define H = moduleCohomology X 1 and P(F) = IsZero(H.obj F). Obtain the cohomological delta-functor from sheafCohomologyAndHigherDirectImages. Its degree-one functor is additive, so it sends the zero module to zero. For a short exact complex use exact_middle in degree one and ShortComplex.Exact.isZero_of_both_isZero to prove extension stability.

proof.text: For r >= 1 choose the zeroth element of Fin r. The inclusion and projection of that summand compose to the identity. Apply H.map_comp and H.map_id; if H of the biproduct is zero, H of the inclusion is zero, hence the identity on H(F) is zero. Thus P(F).

proof.text: For each integral closed subscheme and its generic point, exists_coherent_pushforward_support_eq_range gives F on Y with the prescribed support and annihilator for G = f_*F. Finite pushforward coherence supplies coherence of G. Apply finite_affine_pushforward_ideal_devissage to each monic quasi-coherent ideal inclusion with surjective generic stalk, obtaining precisely condition (3)(c).

proof.text: Apply coherent_property_devissage_integral_subschemes to the zero, extension, summand, and integral hypotheses constructed above. It gives H^1(X,F) = 0 for every coherent F.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YQ (lemma-image-affine-finite-morphism-affine-Noetherian), proof paragraph verifying devissage (3)(c); checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YQ

proof.text: Noetherian X supplies compactness and quasi-separatedness. For any IdealSheafData I of finite type, its module is the kernel of the structure-sheaf map to the closed-subscheme direct image. The structure modules are quasi-coherent; closed-immersion pushforward preserves quasi-coherence, and the proved source quasi-coherent kernel theorem makes I.toModules quasi-coherent. By the locally Noetherian coherence criterion it is coherent. Apply the preceding vanishing to this ideal and then Serre's finite-type ideal criterion.

split_report.summary: Split following Stacks 01YQ and its proof (coherent.tex 3557-3616) in 8 steps: preliminaries (f affine and of finite type, Y locally Noetherian, coherent = quasi-coherent of finite type), the devissage hypotheses (1) by the long exact sequence, (2) by a retraction (functoriality only), (3)(a)(b) from 01YO with G = f_*F coherent by 01Y6, (3)(c) with G' = JG coherent, G'_xi = G_xi, and H^1(X, JG) = H^1(X, f_*(f^{-1}J F)) = H^1(Y, f^{-1}J F) = 0 by 01YP, 089W, 01XB; then the devissage lemma 01YM gives H^1(X,F) = 0 for all coherent F and Serre's criterion 01XG (quasi-separated by 01OY, finite-type ideals coherent by 01XZ) gives X affine. Three new unsplit nodes: the devissage lemma 01YM, Lemma 01YO, Lemma 01YP with the quasi-coherence of f^{-1}I F that 01YQ takes from the proof of 01YP. Tags checked in tags/tags: 01YM (not 01YI), 01YO (not 01YL), 01YP, 01XB, 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology; 01XC is the vanishing of R^p f_*), 01XG.
